title: Read-only on call: Kubernetes with k8sgpt and HolmesGPT
part: Part 3 · AI as your co-admin, behind gates
brief: Three faults in namespace shop, two investigators, zero write verbs. The API server's audit log, not the agent, says what happened.

exercises.prompt: STCLab added runbook exclusion rules to HolmesGPT. Wasted tool calls per investigation went from:
exercises.explain: 16 to 2, with a rubric score of 4.6/5 with runbooks against 3.6/5 without, at about $0.04 per investigation. Their lesson: runbooks over models. The model did not get smarter; they told it what not to do.

exercises.prompt: The lab's ClusterRole for the investigators deliberately omits which of these?
options: get secrets, pods/exec, and every write verb
exercises.explain: Read-only is a verb list on the server. drill.sh prove-ro runs kubectl auth can-i for each identity; every answer on secrets, exec and writes must be no before any agent runs.

exercises.prompt: k8sgpt's --anonymize masks resource names before they reach the model. Which of these does it NOT cover, per its own docs?
options: Pods, logs, events, PVCs and ReplicaSets
exercises.explain: With a cloud backend you are still sending pod names and log lines. With a local model it matters less. Know what your privacy flag actually does.

exercises.prompt: The frontend logs 'connect to catalog.shop.svc:80 failed'. The runbook-free agent will probably blame the network. What is the planted cause?
options: The Service selector says app=catalogue; the pods are labelled app=catalog
exercises.explain: A Service whose selector matches nothing has no endpoints: DNS resolves and every connection is refused. k8sgpt's deterministic analyzer catches it without an LLM; the model only writes the explanation.

exercises.prompt: Run the drill for real. Cleared when the audit summary exists; it must show no write verbs.
exercises.hint: Needs Docker and kind. Compare the holmes-bare and holmes-rb call counts; that is your version of 16 to 2.
